newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty slides ahead of likely NBP action.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty slides ahead of likely NBP action.

text.p: The zloty eased against the basket in early trade as several foreign investors sold Polish treasuries and players lenghtened currency exposure ahead of an expected zloty-depressing central bank intervention.

Dealers said small scale foreign withdrawal along with market expectations that the central bank would step in with a currency-buying operation pulled down the local unit to the key resistance level of three percent from the parity rate.
"The zloty fell as foreign investors sold Polish T-bills and ahead of potential central bank intervention," said Katarzyna Solarz, forex dealer at Pekao SA."
At 0905 GMT the zloty was at 3.06/3.01 percent from the parity rate, down from opening's 3.21/3.15 percent and Thursday's close at 3.24/3.20 percent.
It was at 3.1195/3.1210 to the dollar, down from opening's 3.1130.45 and at 1.8130/40 to the mark, down from 1.8113/28.
Dealers said that after the zloty's pre-emptive slide the central bank would likely refrain from an intervention unless the local unit again rose past 3.10 percent from parity.
On the money market one-day rates inched up after the central bank offered a 200 million zloty drainage and a 600 million NBP-bill sale on Friday.
